app.title: Janaza Guide
home.quran_translation: Every soul will taste death. And you will only receive your full reward on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever is saved from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has truly succeeded. The life of this world is merely the delusion of enjoyment. (3:185)

bathing_corpse.title: Bathing the Deceased
mayyith.title: Deceased Preparation
mayyith.steps_button: Things to Pay Attention to Regarding the Dying Person
mayyith.after_death_content:
1. Close the eyes.
2. Tie the jaw and head
3. Fold and straighten the limbs.
4. Change clothes and dress differently.
5. Cover completely with light cloth.
6. Place something on the stomach.
7. Lay facing the Qibla.)
mayyith.death_news_content:
When someone dies or other calamities befall, it is Sunnah to say إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون and pray for the deceased. The Quran says:
الَّذِينَ إِذَا أَصَابَتْهُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ قَالُوا إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ (البقرة)
(Those who, when afflicted with calamity, say: 'We belong to Allah and to Him we shall return.')
mayyith.death_announcement_content: It is good to inform relatives and friends about the death. This is so that they can all participate in the funeral rites. The Prophet (PBUH) informed the companions about Najashi's death in Ethiopia and prayed the funeral prayer with them. The Prophet (PBUH) used to inform the companions about the martyrdom of Zaid ibn Haritha, Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, and Abdullah ibn Rawaha (RA) in battle.
mayyith.mourning_title: Wailing and Lamenting for the Deceased
mayyith.mourning_content:
Wailing and lamenting for the deceased is prohibited. Weeping and shedding tears without noise and commotion is not wrong. It is a sign of natural human grief. When his son Ibrahim died and when Zainab's daughter Umaimah died, the Prophet (PBUH) wept and sobbed.

However, crying loudly for the dead, loosening hair, beating the face, and tearing clothes to express grief is not permissible. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA) is quoted as saying:
أنا بريئ ممن برئ منه رسول الله ﷺ إن رسول الله برئ من الصالقة والحالقة والشاقة (متفق عليه)
(I have no connection with those whom the Prophet (PBUH) has no connection with. The Prophet (PBUH) has no connection with those who cry loudly (for the dead), those who shave their heads, and those who tear their chests.)
steps.screen_title: Things to Pay Attention to Regarding the Dying Person
steps.screen_subtitle: Things Others Should Pay Attention to Regarding the Dying Person
steps.kalima_desc: لقِّنوا مَوْتاكم لا إلهَ إلَّا اللهُ (مسلم، أبوداود، الترمذي) (Teach your dying ones لا إله إلا الله) as narrated by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA) from the Prophet (PBUH). Once said, it should only be repeated if they speak something else afterward. Do not force them to say it or even ask them to say it.
steps.qibla_title: Lay on Right Side Facing Qibla
steps.qibla_desc: This is the opinion of the majority of scholars. However, Imam Shafi'i (RA) was of the opinion that both feet should be directed towards the Qibla with the head slightly raised and laid flat.
steps.yasin_desc: Recite Surah Yasin near the dying person. Abu Dharr and Abu Darda (RA) narrate that the Prophet (PBUH) said: ا ما منْ ميتٍ يموتُ، فيُقرأُ عندهُ سورةُ ( يس )، إلا هوَّنَ اللهُ عز وجل عليهِ (مسند الفردوس) (Whoever dies and Yasin is recited near them, Allah will surely give them comfort.)
steps.eyes_desc: Close both eyes after death. When Abu Salama (RA) died, the Prophet (PBUH) closed his eyes.
steps.covering_desc: Cover the entire body with a cloth. Aisha (RA) narrated that the blessed body was covered with a striped cloth. The dead body can be kissed. There are reports that the Prophet (PBUH) kissed Uthman ibn Maz'un and Abu Bakr (RA) kissed the Prophet (PBUH) after death.
steps.quick_burial_desc:
Bury the deceased as soon as possible. After visiting Talha ibn Bara'i (RA) who was on his deathbed, the Prophet (PBUH) said:
ني لا أرى طلحة إلا قد حدث فيه الموت فأذنوني به وعجلوا فإنه لا ينبغي لجيفة مسلم أن تحبس بين ظهري أهله (أبوداود) (I think death has occurred to Talha. So inform me and hurry up, for it is not appropriate for a Muslim's body to be kept among his family.)
There is no need to wait for anyone other than the deceased's guardian (legal authority) for burial. Even the guardian should only be waited for if no significant change occurs to the dead body. The Prophet (PBUH) said to Ali (RA):
 يا عليُّ، ثلاثٌ لا تؤخِّرْها: الصَّلاةُ إذا آنَت والجِنازةُ إذا حضَرَت والأيِّمُ إذا وجدَت لها كُفُؤًا 
(O Ali, do not delay three things: prayer when its time comes, funeral when it is present, and widow when she finds a suitable match - Ahmad, Tirmidhi)
steps.debt_desc:
If the deceased has debts, they should be paid off as soon as possible. Only after that can his wealth be distributed. Abu Huraira (RA) narrates that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
 نفس المؤمن مُعلَّقة بدَيْنِه حتى يُقْضَى عنه  (أحمد، ابن ماجه، الترمذي)   
(The soul of a believer remains tied to his debt until it is paid off.)
steps.debt_instructions: The Prophet (PBUH) used to ask other companions to pray for those who died with unpaid debts, rather than praying for them himself.
bathing.men_button: How to Bathe a Male Deceased
bathing.women_button: How to Bathe a Female Deceased
bathing.hadith1_desc: Umm Atiyyah (RA) narrates regarding bathing the deceased:
bathing.hadith1_instructions: (When the daughter died, the Messenger (PBUH) came to us and said: Wash her three or five times, or more if you think necessary, with water and sidr leaves, and put camphor or something of camphor in the last wash. When you finish, inform me. When we finished, we informed him, and he gave us his lower garment and said: Shroud her with it.)
bathing.hadith2_instructions: (Start with her right side and the parts of ablution.)
bathing.tayammum_desc: If water is not available for bathing, or if the deceased has decomposed to the extent that bathing is not possible, or if there are no suitable relatives to bathe the deceased (only men present for a female or only women present for a male), then tayammum should be performed.
bathing.spouse_desc: A husband can bathe his wife and a wife can bathe her husband. Ali (RA) bathed Fatimah (RA).
bathing.spouse_translation: (If I had known then what I know now, none would have washed the Prophet (PBUH) except his wives - Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Hakim)
bathing.children_desc: There is no dispute that women can bathe young boys.
men_bathing.title: How to Bathe a Male Deceased
men_bathing.who_title: Who Should Bathe a Male Deceased?
men_bathing.who_desc:
A male should be bathed by males. However, a husband can bathe his wife and a wife can bathe her husband.

The best people to bathe a male deceased are in this order: father, grandfather, son, grandson, brother, nephew, paternal uncle, their male children, other family members, then other men.
men_bathing.special_desc:
• Clothes should be removed before bathing the deceased. If it's difficult to remove clothes from some bodies, it's better to cut them with scissors or blade.

• If someone dies during Hajj, they should be bathed normally. The shroud should be made from the same ihram clothes they entered ihram with. The head should not be covered and no perfume should be applied.
men_bathing.preparation_desc:
Prepare the necessary water for bathing. Place the deceased on a bed, table, desk or any elevated surface for bathing.

Required items:
• Bucket, cup
• Soap, shampoo
• Washing cloth
• Dettol
• Fragrances like camphor, musk
• Cotton
• Scissors, blade, nail cutter
• Tapes, plasters (to prevent blood and other fluids from coming out)
men_bathing.method_desc:
1. Cover the deceased's private parts with some cloth.

2. Raise the head slightly above the waist and gently massage the stomach. The person bathing should wear gloves or wrap cloth around hands.

3. Clean the private parts.

4. Perform ablution as for prayer.

5. Wash the head and beard with soap.

6. Wash the right side first, then the left side. This should be done three times. If anything comes out again, clean it and wash again.

7. If not clean after three times, it can be washed five or seven times.

8. Dry the body after bathing.

9. Apply fragrance to the places of prostration, private parts, and armpits. It's good to apply to the whole body.

10. Cut mustache and nails if they are long.
men_bathing.complete_desc:
Place the deceased on a bed or plank in a private place away from public view, with the head on the elevated part.

Cover the entire body with cloth. The person bathing should stand on the left side of the deceased. Then support the deceased and place your right knee against the deceased's back on the bed. Hold with the right thumb in the armpit. Press and massage the stomach repeatedly with the left hand.

Sit leaning on the knee and gently massage the stomach with the left hand (this is done to expel everything from the stomach). During this time, the assistant should keep pouring water.

Lay flat and clean the private parts wearing gloves or with cloth wrapped around hands.

After washing hands, wrap another cloth and clean the teeth and nostrils with the left index finger.

Perform ablution as for prayer. Wash the head and beard with sidr, soap or shampoo.

Comb the beard and hair. First wash the right side, then the left side (from head to feet). Then turn to the left side and wash the right back, then turn to the right side and wash the left back. Washing three times is sunnah. If not clean, the number can be increased to five or seven (odd numbers are sunnah).

Use shampoo or soap in the first wash.

After washing away the sidr or soap, pour clean water three times. In this third time, or at the very end, using camphor, musk, and other fragrances is sunnah. Soften the joints and wipe away water with cloth.
women_bathing.title: How to Bathe a Female Deceased
women_bathing.who_title: How to Bathe a Female Deceased
women_bathing.who_desc: A female should be bathed by females. However, a husband can bathe his wife and a wife can bathe her husband.
women_bathing.best_desc: If the deceased is female: mother, grandmother, daughter, granddaughter, paternal aunt, maternal aunt, their daughters, other women, husband.
women_bathing.special_desc:
• If a man dies and only non-related women are present to bathe him, or if a woman dies and only non-related men are present to bathe her, tayammum should be performed in such cases.

• Non-related women should not bathe male deceased, nor should non-related men bathe female deceased.

• Clothes should be removed before bathing the deceased. If it's difficult to remove clothes from some bodies, it's better to cut them with scissors or blade.
women_bathing.hajj_desc: If someone dies during Hajj, they should be bathed normally. The shroud should be made from the same ihram clothes they entered ihram with. The head should not be covered and no perfume should be applied. If it's a woman in ihram, she should wear clothes except for the face and hands, and the same applies to shrouding.
women_bathing.preparation_desc:
Prepare the necessary water for bathing. Place the deceased on a bed, table, desk or any elevated surface for bathing.

Required items:
• Bucket, cup
• Soap, shampoo
• Washing cloth
• Dettol
• Fragrances like camphor, musk
• Cotton
• Scissors, blade, nail cutter
• Tapes, plasters (to prevent blood and other fluids from coming out)
women_bathing.method_desc:
1. Cover the deceased's private parts with some cloth.

2. Raise the head slightly above the waist and gently massage the stomach. The person bathing should wear gloves or wrap cloth around hands.

3. Clean the private parts.

4. Perform ablution as for prayer.

5. Wash the head with soap.

6. Wash the right side first, then the left side. This should be done three times.

7. If not clean after three times, it can be washed five or seven times.

8. Dry the body after bathing.

9. Apply fragrance to the places of prostration, private parts, and armpits. It's good to apply to the whole body.

10. Cut nails if they are long.

11. Divide the woman's hair into three parts and place them at the back.
women_bathing.complete_desc:
Place the deceased on a bed or plank in a private place away from public view, with the head on the elevated part.

Cover the entire body with cloth. The person bathing should stand on the left side of the deceased. Then support the deceased and place your right knee against the deceased's back on the bed.

Hold with the right thumb in the armpit. Press and massage the stomach repeatedly with the left hand. At this time, there's a possibility of excretions coming out from the private parts, so pour plenty of water.

Then lay in the original position. Clean the private parts with cloth wrapped around the left hand. Then clean the teeth with the right hand. Similarly, remove dirt from the nostrils. Then perform complete ablution. However, when rinsing the mouth, tilt the head to prevent water from entering inside.

Remove dirt between nails with a soft stick. Wash the head with water mixed with soap or sidr. Then wash the right front part from chest to feet using soapy water. Then wash the left front part similarly.

Then turn the deceased to the left side and wash the right back part from chest to feet with soapy water. Then turn to the right side and wash the left back part similarly. Then lay flat and pour water once from head to feet.

Then make the intention 'I am giving the obligatory bath' and pour clean water from head to feet three times. In the final stage, water mixed with a little camphor can be poured in the aforementioned manner or by sitting the deceased up. Then dry the entire body with a good cloth.
kafan.mandatory_desc: Wrapping the entire body of the deceased with cloth or other material to cover the whole body is the primary and mandatory method of shrouding.
kafan.procedure_desc:
1. Perfumed cotton can be placed on the eyes, nose, and places of prostration (not sunnah or fard).
2. One cloth is sufficient for shrouding. (Fard)
3. For men, 3 cloths are sunnah.
4. For women, 5 cloths are sunnah.
5. For men – shirt, lower garment, cloth
6. For women – lower garment, shirt, face veil, 2 cloths can be adopted.
7. If only cloths are used, first fold from the left side and fold in a way that the right comes on top like folding hands in prayer.
8. Tie 3 knots so the cloths don't come undone. These should be untied when placing in the grave.
kafan.men_desc:
It is best to shroud a male in three white cloths. No shirt or head covering. The cloths should be wrapped one over the other.

Spread the largest cloth first. Then sprinkle camphor on it and perfume it with fragrances like oud. Then do the same with the second and third cloths. Apply fragrance to the deceased. Lay the deceased on top of it. Place cotton between the buttocks and tie with cloth. Place cotton in all openings of the deceased. Then wrap each cloth, first the right side to the left, then the left side to the right. Do this with each cloth. Place the remaining parts at the feet and head. Tie to prevent loosening. Any type of clothing that was permissible to wear during lifetime can be used for shrouding. However, white cloth is best. One cloth covering the entire body is mandatory. After shrouding, tie at the feet, head, and waist, and untie these knots when placing in the grave.

Boys can be shrouded in one to three cloths.
kafan.women_desc:
A female should be shrouded in five garments. These are a prayer shirt, face veil, lower garment, and two cloths for wrapping.

For a female, a face veil, long shirt, lower garment, and two pieces of cloth that can cover the entire body are best. After dressing in permissible garments, the deceased should be laid on the shroud cloth. Before that, perfumed cotton should be placed in all openings and also on all limbs that touch the ground in prostration. Apply fragrance to the deceased. After shrouding, tie at the feet, head, and waist, and untie these knots when placing in the grave.

For girls, one shirt and two wrapping cloths are sufficient.
kafan.hadith1_desc: Abu Qatada (RA) narrates that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
kafan.hadith1_instructions: (When any of you takes charge of his brother's affairs, let him shroud him well.)
kafan.hadith2_desc: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrates that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
kafan.hadith2_instructions: (Wear white clothes, for they are your best clothes, and shroud your dead in them.)
kafan.hadith3_desc: Jabir (RA) narrates that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
kafan.hadith3_instructions: (When you perfume the deceased, perfume them three times.)
kafan.prophet_instructions: (The Prophet (PBUH) was shrouded in three pieces of new white Sahuli cloth. There was no shirt or turban in it.)
kafan.zainab_instructions: (To shroud daughter Zainab (RA), the Prophet (PBUH) gave them a lower garment, a shirt, a face veil, and two pieces of cloth.)
kafan.hajj_desc: If someone engaged in Hajj dies, they should be bathed like others are bathed. However, they should be shrouded in ihram clothes. The male's head should not be covered nor should fragrance be applied. The state of ihram should continue in his case.
kafan.hajj_translation: (While a man was standing with the Messenger (PBUH) at Arafat, he fell from his mount and broke his neck and died. The incident was reported to the Prophet (PBUH), and he said: Bathe him with water and sidr, shroud him in his two garments, do not apply perfume or cover his head, for Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment in a state of talbiyah.)
kafan.guidelines_desc: The shroud should be moderate and inexpensive. Unnecessary expenses should be avoided. Silk clothing is forbidden for men, so their shroud should not be silk either. Funeral expenses should be borne from the deceased's own wealth. If they have no wealth, those who take responsibility for them should bear the cost. If there are no such people, then from Baitul Mal.
prayer_step_screen.title: Four Takbirs
prayer_step_screen.step1_instructions:
Men should raise their hands up to their ears. Women should raise them up to their shoulders.

After the first Takbir, recite Al-Fatiha.


  بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ ۝١ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ ۝٢ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ ۝٣ مَـٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ ۝٤ إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ ۝٥ ٱهْدِنَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ ۝٦ صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ ۝٧

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all the worlds. The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Master of the Day of Judgment. You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help. Guide us to the straight path. The path of those You have blessed, not of those who have incurred Your wrath, nor of those who have gone astray.
prayer_step_screen.step2_desc: After the second Takbir, recite Salawat upon the Prophet (PBUH).
prayer_step_screen.step2_arabic: اللهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى إبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ اَلَّلهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ
prayer_step_screen.step2_instructions: O Allah, send Your blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent Your blessings upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. O Allah, send Your blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.
prayer_step_screen.step3_desc: After the third Takbir, pray for the deceased.
prayer_step_screen.step3_arabic: اَلَّلهُمَّ أغْفِرْلَهُ وَرْحَمْهُ وَعْفُ عَنْهُ وَعَافِهِ وَاَكْرِمْ نُزُلَهُ وَوَسِّعْ مَدْخَلَهُ وَغْسِلْهُ بِالْمَاءِ وَثَّلْجِ وَالْبَرَدِ وَنَقِّهِ مِنَالْخَطَايَا كَمَا يُنَقَّ الْثَّوْبُ الْاَبْيَضُ مِنَ الدَّنٍَسِ وَاَبْدِلْهُ دَارً خَيْرً مِنْ دَارِهِ وَاَهْلً خَيْرً مِّنْ اَهْلِهِ وَزَوْجً خَيْرًمِّنْ زَوْجِهِ وَاَدْخِلْهُ الْجَنَّتَ وَاَعِذْهُ مِنْ عَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ وَفِتْنَتِهِ وَمِنْ عَذَابِ الْنَّارٍ
prayer_step_screen.step3_instructions: O Allah, forgive him and have mercy on him, pardon him and grant him well-being. Honor his dwelling and make his entrance spacious. Wash him with water, snow and hail, and cleanse him from sins as white cloth is cleansed from dirt. Give him a better home than his home, a better family than his family, and a better spouse than his spouse. Admit him to Paradise and protect him from the punishment of the grave and its trials, and from the punishment of the Fire.
prayer_step_screen.step4_arabic: اَلَّلهُمَّ لاَ تُحَرِّمْنَا اَجْرَهُ وَ لاَ تَفْتِنَّا بَعْدَهُ وَغْفِرْلَنَا وَلَهُ رَبَّنَا اَتِنَا فِي الدُّنْياَ حَسَنَتً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَبَ النَّارِ
prayer_step_screen.step4_instructions:
O Allah, do not deprive us of his reward and do not test us after him. Forgive us and him. Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the next world, and save us from the punishment of the Fire.

Then say 'Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh' and give salam.
salat_janaza.title: Funeral Prayer
salat_janaza.social_obligation_desc: Funeral prayer is a social obligation. If some members of the community perform it, everyone else is relieved of the obligation.
salat_janaza.social_obligation_arabic: إن النبي كان يؤتى بالرجل المتوفى عليه الدين فيسأل هل ترك لدينه فضلا، فإن حدث أنه ترك وفاء صلى، وإلا قال للمسلمين: صلوا لى صاحبكم
salat_janaza.social_obligation_translati: (A man who died with debt would be brought to the Prophet (PBUH). He would ask if he left anything to pay his debt. If it was said that he left enough to pay it, he would pray for him. Otherwise, he would say to the Muslims: Pray for your companion - Bukhari, Muslim)
salat_janaza.reward_importance_desc: Funeral prayer is a very important matter.
salat_janaza.reward_importance_hadith: Abu Huraira (RA) narrates that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
salat_janaza.reward_importance_arabic: من تبع جنازة وصلى عليها فله قيراط ومن تبعها حتى يفرغ منها فله قيراطان أحدهما مثل أحد
salat_janaza.reward_importance_translati: (Whoever follows a funeral and prays for it will have one qirat of reward. Whoever follows it until he is finished with it will have two qirats, one of which is equal to Mount Uhud.)
salat_janaza.mandatory_elements_desc: All the prerequisites for other prayers apply to funeral prayer except for timing. The mandatory elements of funeral prayer are as follows:
salat_janaza.mandatory_elements_list:
1) Intention
2) Standing if able
3) Four takbirs
4) Recite Al-Fatiha after the first takbir
5) Recite salawat upon the Prophet (PBUH) after the second takbir
6) Pray for the deceased after the third takbir
7) Give salam after the fourth takbir
salat_janaza.four_takbir_arabic: إن النبي ﷺ صلى على النجاشي فكبر أربعا
salat_janaza.four_takbir_translation: (The Prophet (PBUH) prayed for Najashi and said four takbirs.) - Bukhari, Muslim
salat_janaza.prayer_method_hadith: Imam Shafi'i (RA) narrates in his Musnad that Abu Umamah ibn Sahl (RA) said that a companion told him:
salat_janaza.prayer_method_arabic: إن السنة في الصلاة على الجنازة أن يكبر الإمام ثم يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب بعد ويخلص الدعاء التكبيرة الأولى سرا في نفسه ثم يصلي على النبي في الجنازة في التكبيرات ولا يقرأ في شيئ منهن ثم يسلم سرا في نفسه
salat_janaza.prayer_method_translation: (The Sunnah in funeral prayer is that the imam says takbir, then recites Al-Fatiha quietly after the first takbir, then sends salawat upon the Prophet, then prays sincerely for the deceased after the takbirs without reciting Quran in any of them, then gives salam quietly.)
salat_janaza.sincere_prayer_desc: The imam should say the takbirs and salam aloud. The followers should say them quietly like in other prayers. The same salawat recited in tashahhud in regular prayers should be recited in funeral prayer. Any prayer for the good of the deceased is acceptable, but the prayer mentioned in hadith is best.
salat_janaza.sincere_prayer_arabic: إذا صليتم على الميت فأخلصوا له الدعاء
salat_janaza.sincere_prayer_translation: (When you pray for the deceased, be sincere in your supplication for him.) - Abu Dawud, Bayhaqi, Ibn Hibban
salat_janaza.leadership_desc: According to Imam Shafi'i (RA), the leadership of funeral prayer should be in the following order:
salat_janaza.leadership_list:
1) Father 
2) Grandfather
3) Son
4) Son's son
5) Brother
6) Brother's son
7) Paternal uncle
8) Paternal uncle's son
prayers_hadith.title: Prayers in Hadith
prayers_hadith.hadith1_desc: Abu Huraira (RA) narrates that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
prayers_hadith.hadith1_arabic: إِذَا صَلَّيْتُمْ عَلَى الْمَيِّتِ فَأَخْلِصُوا لَهُ الدُّعَاءَ
prayers_hadith.hadith1_translation: (When you pray for the deceased, be sincere in your supplication for him.)
prayers_hadith.hadith2_desc: Abu Ibrahim (RA) narrates that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
prayers_hadith.hadith2_arabic: مَا مِنْ رَجُلٍ مُسْلِمٍ يَمُوتُ فَيَقُومُ عَلَى جَنَازَتِهِ أَرْبَعُونَ رَجُلاً لاَ يُشْرِكُونَ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا إِلاَّ شَفَّعَهُمُ اللَّهُ فِيهِ
prayers_hadith.hadith2_translation: (No Muslim man dies and forty men who associate nothing with Allah stand for his funeral prayer, but Allah will accept their intercession for him.)
prayers_hadith.hadith3_desc: Malik ibn Hubayra (RA) narrates that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
prayers_hadith.hadith3_arabic: مَا مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ يَمُوتُ فَيُصَلِّي عَلَيْهِ ثَلاَثَةُ صُفُوفٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ إِلاَّ أَوْجَبَ
prayers_hadith.hadith3_translation: (No Muslim dies and three rows of Muslims pray for him but it makes (Paradise) certain for him.)
samshaya.title: Frequently Asked Questions
samshaya.q1_title: Question 1: Where can Janaza prayer be performed?
samshaya.q1_answer: Janaza prayer can be performed in the mosque or outside the mosque in any clean place. The Prophet (PBUH) performed Janaza prayer both inside and outside the mosque.
samshaya.q2_title: Question 2: Can women participate in Janaza prayer?
samshaya.q2_answer: Women can participate in Janaza prayer. However, they should stand behind the men. Women like Umm Atiyyah (RA) participated in Janaza prayers.
samshaya.q3_title: Question 3: Can Janaza prayer be performed for children?
samshaya.q3_answer: Janaza prayer can be performed for children who were born and cried. The Prophet (PBUH) performed Janaza prayer for children. However, Janaza prayer is not required for children who were born but did not cry.
samshaya.q4_title: Question 4: Is ablution required for Janaza prayer?
samshaya.q4_answer: Ablution is required for Janaza prayer. Since it is a prayer, all conditions of other prayers apply to it as well.
samshaya.q5_title: Question 5: How many times can Janaza prayer be performed?
samshaya.q5_answer: Janaza prayer can only be performed once for one deceased. However, those who could not participate in the first Janaza can perform it separately later.
samshaya.q6_title: Question 6: Can Ghaiban prayer (prayer in absentia) be performed?
samshaya.q6_answer: Ghaiban prayer is performing Janaza prayer without the deceased being present. The Prophet (PBUH) performed Ghaiban prayer for Najashi in Ethiopia. This is permissible in special circumstances.
janaza_samskaranam.title: Funeral Rites
janaza_samskaranam.step1_desc: The funeral process should be expedited as much as possible. The same applies to carrying the deceased to the burial ground. Do not walk slowly, but walk with some haste.
janaza_samskaranam.step1_arabic: لقد رأيتنا مع رسول الله ﷺ وسلم وإنا لنكاد نرمل بالجنازة رملا
janaza_samskaranam.step1_translation: I saw us walking quickly with the funeral procession alongside the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) - Ahmad, Nasa'i
janaza_samskaranam.step2_title: How to Carry the Funeral Bier
janaza_samskaranam.step2_desc: Ramal is walking with shoulders moving and with haste. It is better to support the funeral bier from all sides rather than holding it from the four corners.
janaza_samskaranam.step2_arabic: من اتبع جنازة فليحمل بجوانب السرير كلها فإنه من السنة
janaza_samskaranam.step2_translation: Whoever follows a funeral should carry from all sides of the bier, for that is the Sunnah.
janaza_samskaranam.step3_title: How to Walk with the Funeral Procession
janaza_samskaranam.step3_desc: Those walking should move in front, behind, to the right, and to the left of the funeral bier. Those traveling by vehicle should follow behind.
janaza_samskaranam.step3_arabic: الراكب خلف الجنازة والماشي خلفها وأمامها وعن يمينها و عن يسارها قريبا منها والسقط يصلى عليه ويدعى لوالديه بالمغفرة والرحمة
janaza_samskaranam.step3_translation: The rider should be behind the funeral, and the walker should be behind it, in front of it, to its right and to its left, close to it. Prayer should be offered for the stillborn, and forgiveness and mercy should be sought for its parents.
janaza_samskaranam.step3_source: Mughirah ibn Shu'bah (RA) narrates that the Prophet (PBUH) said
janaza_samskaranam.step4_title: Things Not to Do with the Funeral
janaza_samskaranam.step4_desc:
1. Raising voice in dhikr, reciting Quran, etc.
2. Do not carry fire with the funeral
3. Those accompanying the funeral should not sit before the funeral is placed down
4. Women should not follow the funeral
janaza_samskaranam.step4_arabic: كان أصحاب رسول الله ﷺﷺ يكرهون رفع الصوت عند ثلاث: عند الجنائز وعند الذكر وعند القتال
janaza_samskaranam.step4_translation: The companions of the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) disliked raising voices in three situations: at funerals, during dhikr, and in battle.
janaza_samskaranam.step5_desc: Burying the deceased is a social obligation of Muslims. There is nothing wrong with burying at night. During the time of the Prophet (PBUH) and the companions, the deceased were buried at night as well as during the day.
janaza_samskaranam.step6_desc: The body should be concealed in the earth so that no foul smell emerges when it decomposes, and wild animals cannot dig it out. This is what burial aims to achieve. It is good to make the grave deep.
janaza_samskaranam.step7_title: How to Lower the Deceased into the Grave
janaza_samskaranam.step7_desc: The deceased should be lowered into the grave feet first. The deceased should be laid on the right side with the face turned towards the Qibla. The knots of the shroud should be untied.
janaza_samskaranam.step8_desc: After burial, one should pray for the deceased's forgiveness and for steadfastness when questioned.
janaza_samskaranam.step8_arabic: استغفروا لأخيكم وسلوا له التثبيت فإنه الآن يسأل
janaza_samskaranam.step8_translation: Seek forgiveness for your brother and ask for steadfastness for him, for he is now being questioned.
janaza_samskaranam.step9_desc: It is good to place a stone or other marker on the grave for identification purposes.
janaza_samskaranam.step9_arabic: أتعلم بها قبر أخي وأدفن إليه من مات من أهلي
janaza_samskaranam.step9_translation: By this I will recognize my brother's grave and bury near it those of my family who die.
after_janaza.step1_desc:
Consoling the grieving family of the deceased is Sunnah, even if the deceased is a non-Muslim. All family members - men, women, elders, and children - can be consoled without distinction. This can be done before or after the burial. Generally, the time for Ta'ziyah is up to three days. If someone couldn't do it due to travel or other reasons, it can be done even after three days.

Any words that provide comfort and encourage patience and forbearance can be used in Ta'ziyah. Scholars have quoted the following as words of consolation.

The consoled person should say 'Ameen' and say to the consoler 'Ajrakallah' (May Allah reward you!).

Both should part after saying words of consolation.

According to Imam Shafi'i, gathering for Ta'ziyah and preparing food for this purpose is an un-Islamic practice (Bid'ah). The same applies to the practices of Chavadi Anthiram (death anniversary gatherings) and celebrations on the 15th, 40th, and annual days that are common in many places. None of these have precedent in the Prophet's practice.
after_janaza.step1_arabic: أعظم الله أجرك وأحسن عزائك وغفر لميتك
after_janaza.step1_translation: May Allah grant you the best reward, give you good consolation, and forgive your deceased!
after_janaza.step2_desc:
Visiting graves is Sunnah for men. Going near the grave, greeting the deceased, and praying to Allah for their forgiveness - this is what is intended by grave visitation. It helps the visitor increase their awareness of the afterlife. Graves of criminals and disbelievers can also be visited for this purpose. In the early period of Islam, the Prophet (ﷺ) had prohibited grave visitation. The reason was the possibility of shirk-related practices entering the visitation. Later, the prohibition was lifted. Buraida (RA) narrates that the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

كنت نهيتكم عن زيارة القبور ألا فزوروها فإنها تذكر كم الآخرة

I had prohibited you from visiting graves. Now visit them, for they remind you of the afterlife.

The following hadiths clarify what should be said during grave visitation.

1) Buraida (RA) says:

كان النبي ﷺﷺ يعلمهم إذا خرجوا إلى المقابر أن يقول قائلهم: السلام عليكم أهل الديار من المؤمنين والمسلمين وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون. أنتم فرطنا ونحن لكم تبع ونسأل الله لنا ولكم العافية

The Prophet (ﷺ) used to teach them to say this when they went to cemeteries: Peace be upon you, O inhabitants of this abode from among the believers and Muslims. If Allah wills, we will join you. You have preceded us and we are following you. We ask Allah for well-being for us and for you.

2) Aisha (RA) says:

قلت : كيف أقول لهم يا رسول الله ؟ قال : قولي : السلام على أهل الديار من المؤمنين والمسلمين ويرحم الله المستقدمين منا والمستأخرين وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون

I asked: O Messenger of Allah, what should I say to them? He said: Say:

السلام على أهل الديار من المؤمنين والمسلمين ويرحم الله المستقدمين منا والمستأخرين وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون

Other hadiths have also come regarding this. However, touching and kissing the grave, circumambulating it, prostrating on it, etc., are shirk-related acts and are prohibited.

Not only men, but women can also visit the graves of their relatives. This is provided they don't wail at the grave or engage in other un-Islamic practices. If they do so, it becomes a cause of curse for them. When Aisha (RA) returned from visiting the grave of her brother Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Bakr (RA), Abdullah ibn Mulaik (RA) happened to see her. He asked:

يا أم المؤمنين من أين أقبلت ؟ قالت : من قبر أخي عبد الرحمن فقلت كان لها أليس كان نهى رسول اللہ ﷺ عن زيارة القبور ؟ قالتنهى عن زيارة القبور ثم أمر بزيارتها

O Mother of the Believers, where are you coming from? She said: From my brother Abdur Rahman's grave. Then I asked her: Didn't the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prohibit visiting graves? She said: Yes, he prohibited visiting graves, then he commanded to visit them.
after_janaza.step3_desc: Prayers to be recited during grave visitation:
after_janaza.step3_arabic: السلام عليكم أهل الديار من المؤمنين والمسلمين وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون. أنتم فرطنا ونحن لكم تبع ونسأل الله لنا ولكم العافية
after_janaza.step3_translation: Peace be upon you, O inhabitants of this abode from among the believers and Muslims. If Allah wills, we will join you. You have preceded us and we are following you. We ask Allah for well-being for us and for you.
after_janaza.step4_desc:
Any good deed done by a Muslim during their lifetime will benefit them after death. However, there are three things that remain permanent and continue to yield results.

These are: continuous charity, beneficial knowledge, and righteous children who pray for them.

1. Charity:
Charity done especially by children for the deceased also benefits them. Abu Huraira (RA) narrates:

ان رجلا قال للنبي ﷺ إن أبي مات وترك مالا ولم يوص فهل يكفر عنه أن أتصدق عنه ؟ قال : نعم

A man approached the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked: My father has died. He left wealth but made no will. Will it expiate his sins if I give charity on his behalf? The Prophet (ﷺ) said: Yes.

2. Hajj:
If the deceased had an obligation to perform Hajj, and the children perform it on their behalf, they will receive its reward. Ibn Abbas (RA) narrates:

إن امرأة من جهينة جائت إلى النبي ﷺ فقالت: أن أمي نذرت أن تحج فلم تحج حتى ماتت أفأحج عنها ؟ قال : حجي عنها. أرأيت لو كان على أمك دين أكنت قاضيته ؟ اقضوا فالله أحق بالقضاء

A woman from the Juhayna tribe came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: My mother vowed to perform Hajj but couldn't do it before she died. Should I perform Hajj on her behalf? He said: Perform Hajj for her. If your mother had a debt, wouldn't you pay it? Pay the debt, for Allah is most deserving of having debts paid.

3. Fasting:
The same applies to fasting. Ibn Abbas (RA) narrates:

جاء رجل إلى النبي ﷺ فقال : يا رسول الله إن أمي ماتت وعليها صوم شهر أفأقضيه عنها ؟ قال : لو كان على أمك دين أكنت قاضيه عنها ؟

A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, my mother has died and she owed a month of fasting. Should I fast on her behalf? The Prophet (ﷺ) asked: If your mother had a debt, would you pay it for her? He said: Yes. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: Then Allah's debt is most deserving to be paid.

4. Quran Recitation:
There is no evidence in the Quran for reciting the Quran and donating its reward to the deceased or anyone living. There is no example from the Prophet (ﷺ) either. Imam Shafi'i's famous opinion is that doing so yields no reward. Ahmad ibn Hanbal and other scholars are of the opinion that it does yield reward. Even those who say it benefits stipulate that the person who recited the Quran should not take any reward for it. The result of the recitation should be considered as donated to the deceased. Many later scholars opine that such donation in the name of the Prophet (ﷺ) is not desirable. There is no evidence that any of the Companions made such donations in the name of the Prophet (ﷺ).
after_janaza.step4_arabic: إذا مات ابن آدم انقطع عمله إلا من ثلاث صدقة جارية أو علم ينتفع به أو ولد صالح يدعوله
after_janaza.step4_source: Abu Huraira (RA) narrates that the Prophet (ﷺ) said
after_janaza.step5_title: Transporting the Deceased to Another Country and Embalming
after_janaza.step5_desc:
Transporting the deceased to another country is not permissible in Islam. Only a very weak opinion validates this transportation. This doesn't apply to embalming and transporting either. However, when sending the deceased to their homeland, embalming is done to prevent decay during transport.

What is embalming?
Embalming involves extracting the deceased's blood from veins using surgical instruments and then injecting embalming chemicals into the body. For this, a vein near the deceased's neck, or in the case of a woman, a vein in the thigh area, is cut and a tube is attached. Blood is extracted through a pump and the following chemicals are injected:

1. Formaldehyde, 2. Glutaraldehyde, 3. Methanol, 4. Ethanol. Those without much knowledge of chemistry need to understand one thing here. Ethanol is alcohol or liquor. Into the body of someone for whom alcohol was haram in life, we are forcibly injecting alcohol through veins after death without their consent. What evils are involved in this process?

1. Mutilating the deceased (Haram).
2. Delaying burial (against Sunnah). Often the deceased reaches home after five or six days (sometimes even more).
3. Unnecessarily creating wounds in the deceased's body (Haram).
4. Extracting blood (Haram).
5. Injecting foreign substances, including alcohol (Haram).

Now tell me, what satisfaction do we relatives get from seeing bluish, disfigured corpses?

At the same time, when someone who has been living as an expatriate away from family for a long time dies, relatives certainly have a desire to see the deceased one last time. In such circumstances, if it's possible to preserve the body without the aforementioned methods and get it home without much delay, that can be understood as acceptable.
